内容: Ultimately, they coalesced into three main groups, each proposing a solution that would let a minuscule socialist movement overpower the Czarist establishment.

内容: As such, they redefined ‘proletariat’ to include peasants alongside urban factory workers.

内容: Nevertheless, this meant that the Mensheviks would team up with well-funded bourgeois movements who also wanted to overpower the Czarist establishment, albeit for liberal rather than socialist change.

内容: By riding on their coattails, the Mensheviks hoped to acquire goodwill or even power, which they could then use to achieve some socialism within Russia.

内容: Then, there was the ‘Bolshevik’ faction of the Russian Social Democratic Labor Party – the group headed by Lenin.

内容: Like the Mensheviks, the Bolsheviks also focused on the urban factory worker and their current low consciousness.

内容: But unlike them and contrary to classical Marxism, the Bolsheviks did not believe that socioeconomic development was the only way to raise consciousness.

内容: Instead, Lenin argued that, rather than waiting for workers to become disillusioned with capitalism, a movement could artificially and prematurely raise their consciousness.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: If done right, that meant workers would become high consciousness without first needing liberal regimes or mass industrialization.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: In other words, a socialist revolution could happen in Czarist Russia right now.

内容: And in choosing this approach, Lenin would revolutionize movement strategy forever.

内容: At first glance, the Bolshevik proposal to artificially raise consciousness might seem like just another heretical interpretation of Marx.

内容: In fact, what they proposed was a completely different movement grand strategy.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Earlier, we said that movements do 2 things: raise issues to promote public participation, and create organizations to convert participation into power.

内容: From this, we can derive 3 movement grand strategies: 1 focused purely on issues, 1 purely on organization, and 1 combining the 2.

内容: For this entry, we’ll be focusing on the first and third grand strategies.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: What the SRs and Mensheviks were doing was the issue-focused grand strategy, known as the ‘Spontaneous Uprising’.

内容: In it, a movement finds an issue so appealing to the public that they participate in droves, forming a sheer weight of numbers that overpowers establishment resistance.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: As the Socialist Issue was not attractive enough to do this in 1917 Russia, the SRs and Mensheviks had to partner with other movements to achieve the necessary size – the peasants for the SRs, the bourgeoisie for the Mensheviks.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Such partnerships inevitably diluted the change that these socialists hoped to bring to society, but they felt they had no other choice.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: To an ideologue like Lenin, diluting socialism was abhorrent, and so copying the SR or Menshevik partnerships was a non-starter.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: But that meant that the Bolsheviks needed an alternative pathway towards movement success: after all, the only way a Spontaneous Uprising can win is through sheer size, because the typical participant will not sacrifice very much for a cause, and therefore will not generate much power.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Large numbers can still multiply this into something establishment-threatening, but Lenin was now rejecting this because of ideological purity.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: So what was his solution?

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Lenin’s solution began with the profound industrial-age insight that a movement didn’t have to accept everything within its environment as fixed.

内容: Like everything in strategy, environmental factors will always limit a movement’s potential: for example, the public will only find certain issues relevant, and participants will only generate so much power.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: The small proletariat and their lack of consciousness were, of course, major environmental constraints on socialism in 1917 Russia.

内容: The SR and Menshevik strategies worked within these limits.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: The Bolsheviks, by contrast, believed that said limits could be manipulated, and that industrial technology made this task easier than ever before: for example, by manipulating information through propaganda, an issue can become relevant to participants who wouldn’t have ‘naturally’ cared before.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Here, Lenin believed that he could manipulate consciousness growth within the Russian proletariat, and in so doing, prematurely mold them into exceptionally-committed participants, ready to make the large sacrifices necessary for powerful actions, up to and including socialist revolution.

内容: If done right, the small Bolshevik movement would generate a power vastly larger than its size, freeing it from the need to partner with non-socialists in order to achieve success.

内容: To manipulate effectively, the Bolsheviks would need a level of coordination and effort higher than mere individual initiative, and so Lenin saw the need to organize participants in order to direct their actions.

内容: This conscious use of organization to manipulate the environment is a core theme of Lenin’s strategy; but at the same time, Lenin still saw limits to its use, if only because organizations cost resources.

内容: Lenin wasn’t out to manipulate everything, just the consciousness of the proletariat, who were at least considered latent followers of the Socialist Issue.

内容: The Bolsheviks weren’t trying to convert non-proletarians, nor were they actively organizing for a rebellion.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: The point was to raise proletarian consciousness to such an extent that they would see the need for revolution and carry it out themselves.

来源: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (Mar-Nov 1917) | Strategy of Protest and Revolution 4.5 [13/4/2023]
内容: Lenin’s combination of organization and issue resulted in a new grand strategy, which this video series has called ‘Mass Agitation’.

内容: Under Mass Agitation, a movement uses organization to boost the power generated from existing participants, sometimes by coordinating or leading action, other times – as the Bolsheviks did here – by increasing their level of commitment.

内容: If done right, Mass Agitations can win without achieving large amounts of support: not only can this be easier, but perhaps more importantly, it also allows a movement to maintain ideological purity.

内容: Next, we turn to how Lenin saw Mass Agitation working in practice.

内容: Under a grand strategy of Mass Agitation, Lenin theorized that his Bolshevik movement could grow in power by using organized manipulation to artificially raise proletarian consciousness.

内容: Now, it was time to apply theory to reality.

内容: Instead, Lenin opted for a more low-key action that he expected would be less provocative and therefore more sustainable: ‘Agitation’.

内容: Agitation was to be conducted using existing methods: primarily face-to-face conversations and newspapers, several of which Lenin founded.

内容: Through them, the Bolsheviks hoped to manipulate information in such a way as to ‘awaken’ the Russian worker to the true nature of capitalist exploitation, thereby creating the high consciousness proletariat required for movement victory.
